agent_vs_you: The agent correctly chose crop with fit: contain (a 5:3 photo whose sneaker spans ~80% of the width cannot be cropped to a square without cutting it). But it explicitly asked for 'a blurred copy of the photo' as the fill, although the user said 'don't ... change anything else' and the catalogue line for crop says to add 'plain' when the user wants nothing added. It defaulted to the decorative option instead of weighing the user's 'change nothing' against the two fills offered. I would fit the whole, unscaled-in-shape photo into the square with plain bands, so every original pixel stays and nothing new or decorative appears.

your_plan.say: Your sneaker fills most of the photo's width, so a square can't be cut from it without losing the toe or heel. I'll fit the whole photo into the square unchanged and fill the strips above and below with a plain colour, nothing else added.

params.prompt_or_change: Fit the whole photo, unstretched, inside a square; fill the space above and below with a plain colour matching the photo's edges; add nothing else.

steps.why: Code, 0 credits: keeps every original pixel and the sneaker's proportions; plain bands are the 'nothing added' fill the user asked for.

fix: 1) Planner/catalogue: make 'plain' the default for crop fit: contain whenever the user says don't change anything, keep it as is, nothing added, or gives no fill preference; use the blurred copy only when asked ('blurred background'). Reword the crop line: 'fit: contain fills with plain bands of the photo's edge colour; add blur only when the user asks for it'. 2) Harness (crop.js): with plain, sample the top band's colour from the top edge and the bottom band's from the bottom edge (here 0x95958b above, 0xbbc0c5 floor below) instead of one top-edge colour for both, so the bands continue the wall and floor. 3) Longer term: an outpaint/expand tool that keeps the original pixels and extends wall and floor, the professional answer to 'square without cropping'.
evidence: product-sneaker.jpg is 640x384 (5:3); the white sneaker spans x~76-582, 507 px, wider than the largest square crop (384), so some fill is unavoidable. product-sneaker-square.png is 640x640: the full original photo scaled to 640 wide in the middle, sneaker intact and unstretched, with 128 px bands above and below that are a heavily blurred, enlarged copy of the cluttered background (bags, cabinet, wall). The judge's other four must-haves were met; the one fail is exactly the blurred bands, a treatment the user ruled out with 'don't change anything else' and the catalogue's 'plain' option avoids.
